title: Tie-break weights that tell every plan apart

blocks.text: A gas utility chooses which leak sensors to install from a short list of at most twenty, and breaks ties between equally good choices with a small bonus $`\varepsilon \sum_i w_i x_i`$. For the bonus to pick exactly one choice, no two different selections may have the same total weight; and for the choice to repeat, the weights must be the same in every run.

Write `separating_weights(ids)`. It returns a dict giving each sensor id a positive integer weight such that every two different selections of ids have different totals. The weights must not depend on the order of `ids` or on the Python process. Use the powers of two the lesson describes, in sorted id order: the first id gets 1, the next 2, then 4, and so on up to $`2^{n-1}`$ for $`n`$ ids. (Other separating weights exist, some with a smaller largest weight, such as 3, 5, 6 and 7 for four ids; the tests accept any that separate every selection and keep the largest weight at most $`2^{n-1}`$.)

print("same sites, other order:", separating_weights(["K-15", "K-30", "K-07"]))
print("weights for one site:", separating_weights(["K-99"]))
